newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firmer, Delifrance shines.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firmer, Delifrance shines.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Thursday with small stocks and U.S. dollar denominated stocks leading the gainers.
Baker Delifrance hit a new high of S$1.87 after announcing a new joint venture franchise in Indonesia. At 0207 GMT, it had eased to S$1.86, up 18 cents with more than 700,000 shares changing hands.
Dealers said general market sentiment remained upbeat, but there was some profit taking in counters which had run up sharply in recent days.
"The market looks strong, especially in U.S. dollar stocks, but some of my clients are taking profit," said a trader with a Singapore brokerage
The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 4.34 points at 1,979.03. Total market volume was an active 75.58 million units with 225 gainers overwhelming 36 losers.
Leading the actives was Chinese drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin, which touched a new high of US$1.72 in active dealings.
"I think it is overdone, but there is market talk of a US$2 target," a broker said.
Creative Technologies led the gainers, touching another new high of S$36.30 on expectations of strong earnings.
Ship-repair conglomerate Keppel Corp continued to see some selling pressure. It was down five cents at S$6.55 with 2.8 million changing hands.
